questions.question: Why should an `` with `role='presentation'` NOT be flagged as a violation?
choices: Decorative images are exempt from accessibility laws
role='presentation' tells screen readers to skip the image, so no alt is needed
The image is hidden from all users
questions.explanation: A decorative image with `role='presentation'` signals to screen readers that the image has no informational value and should be skipped. Requiring alt text here would be a false positive.

questions.question: What distinguishes an 'error' from a 'warning' in accessibility violations?
choices: Errors are legal violations; warnings are style preferences
Errors block access for users; warnings degrade experience but don't block
Errors are for images; warnings are for text
questions.explanation: Missing alt text on an image blocks screen reader users from understanding the content (error). A heading skip degrades the document structure but doesn't completely block access (warning).

questions.question: Why must accessibility violation reports include line numbers?
choices: Line numbers make reports look more professional
They help developers find and fix the exact location of the violation
Line numbers are required by WCAG
They're only needed for multi-file projects
questions.explanation: A violation report without line numbers forces developers to search manually for the issue. Line numbers make reports actionable by pointing directly to the problem.
